purpose: Fresh multimodal practical gate for the frozen Automotive Commercial Capture Direction extension. Evaluator observations and exact keys were fixed after media acquisition/inspection and before any candidate artifact call.

evaluator.grading: mechanical exact choice comparison against evaluator-owned preregistered keys
evaluator.first_scored_mismatch: REVISE and stop; no scored retry
evaluator.observation_freeze_rule: all media observations below were written before any candidate saw these artifacts

cases.function: Assess this supplied image as a candidate primary listing hero for selling a used vehicle. Judge only what is visible. Choose one option per question.
evaluator_visible_observations_not_candi: Front three-quarter vehicle view is readable.
A second vehicle occupies much of the left background and display/sign material is visible through/on the subject windshield.
Glossy black surfaces contain substantial environment reflections; some describe curvature/body form while other reflected/highlight elements add visual clutter.
The image does not establish the capture device or unseen vehicle condition.

questions.prompt: For the stated primary listing hero function, what is the correct disposition?

options.text: Accept as a clean primary listing hero with no meaningful capture issue.
Reject for primary hero use and plan a cleaner reshoot; the vehicle is visible but the frame is not clean enough for that function.
Treat this single image as complete vehicle-condition proof.

questions.prompt: How should the visible reflections be judged?

options.text: The vehicle surfaces are effectively reflection-free.
All reflections erase the vehicle's form and therefore every reflection should be removed.
The reflections are mixed: some help reveal glossy form/curvature while others are distracting; manage geometry rather than applying a universal no-reflection rule.

questions.prompt: What is the most important visible background judgment?

options.text: Adjacent vehicle/display elements compete with the subject, so the product is not cleanly isolated.
The background is a clean isolated product backdrop.
No background is visible enough to affect the shot.

questions.prompt: What should be corrected first on a reshoot?

options.text: Increase saturation before changing capture geometry.
Clean the background and adjust car/camera geometry to control reflections while preserving useful body-form highlights; then fine-tune exposure/settings.
Add camera movement even though this is a still-photo hero task.

questions.prompt: What device-specific instruction is justified from this artifact alone?

options.text: Assume an iPhone Pro and require Apple Log.
Infer exact shutter and lens settings from the visible pixels and mandate them.
Do not invent device-specific settings; verify the current equipment packet first.

cases.function: Assess this supplied video as candidate sales media for presenting a specific used vehicle. Judge only what the footage establishes. Choose one option per question.
evaluator_visible_observations_not_candi: Footage is a forward road/tunnel driving view at night/twilight; the environment moves through frame while the viewpoint is broadly fixed relative to the recording vehicle.
The vehicle being sold is not shown with exterior/interior/condition coverage sufficient for product identification or proof.
The scene has very dark regions and bright road/tunnel light sources, limiting product readability for a vehicle-sale function.
The finished footage alone does not establish that a driver handheld a phone or otherwise used an unsafe capture method.
The file is 854x332, 30 fps, 22.3 seconds; device identity remains unknown.

questions.prompt: Does the footage provide sufficient vehicle coverage for primary sale hero or condition proof?

options.text: Yes; it provides sufficient full-vehicle sale coverage.
No; the vehicle product itself is insufficiently shown for primary hero or condition-proof use.
Yes; it is equivalent to a complete exterior walk-around.

questions.prompt: What is the most defensible current sales-content use, if any?

options.text: Condition proof of body panels and defects.
Primary vehicle listing hero.
At most atmospheric/route driving B-roll when that supports a concept; not product proof.

questions.prompt: What visible lighting/exposure condition matters for the stated vehicle-sale function?

options.text: High-contrast low-light footage with bright practical lights limits product readability.
Even daylight illumination makes all vehicle details clearly readable.
The body paint is visibly overexposed across a complete exterior view.

questions.prompt: Which description best matches the visible camera/view behavior?

options.text: An orbiting exterior camera continuously reveals the whole car.
A broadly fixed forward-facing viewpoint with road/environment motion through the frame.
A handheld stationary walk-around of the vehicle.

questions.prompt: What safety claim is justified from the finished footage alone?

options.text: Assert that the driver was holding a phone while driving.
Assert the exact mount/rig used even though it is not shown.
Do not infer unsafe driver camera operation or an exact rig from footage that does not establish it; any future capture plan must still use a safe controlled method.

questions.prompt: What is the highest-value next capture change for selling the vehicle?

options.text: Capture the vehicle itself from controlled external/static or safely rigged product-revealing views, chosen for the required hero/proof function.
Add more tunnel footage without changing product visibility.
Digitally zoom farther into the road ahead.

questions.prompt: What device-specific setting can be mandated from this video alone?

options.text: Require Apple ProRes because the footage must have come from an iPhone Pro.
None beyond visible file properties; verify the actual equipment packet before prescribing device-specific capture modes.
Assume the camera supports every modern Log/HDR mode.

claim_boundary: This gate qualifies observation-driven still/video capture judgment on the two frozen real artifacts. It does not replace an applied human-operated AM Motors/iPhone field test for instruction executability and reshoot improvement.
